panels.rationale: Single, clear human fundus photograph showing arrow-labeled Hollenhorst plaques (cholesterol emboli) at retinal arteriolar bifurcations. The caption and disease-focused article explicitly attribute this finding to systemic atheroembolism and AERD. [raw subtype: systemic atheroembolism]
panels.attribution_text: Tan et al. Recurrent Acute Kidney Injury Due to Atheroembolic Renal Disease: Diagnostic Utility of Fundoscopy.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.91523. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Fundus photograph demonstrating Hollenhorst plaques This fundus photograph shows refractile, yellow-gold cholesterol emboli (Hollenhorst plaques, indicated by arrows) located at the bifurcations of retinal arterioles. This finding suggests ophthalmologic evidence of systemic atheroembolism.
in_text_mentions: A third episode of severe AKI (creatinine 591 μmol/L) occurred one month after that, accompanied by anemia and abdominal pain. A CT aortogram showed an enlarging AAA with penetrating ulcers. Fundoscopic examination revealed Hollenhorst plaques, confirming the diagnosis of AERD (Figure 3). Upon this diagnosis, apixaban was discontinued to prevent further cholesterol crystal embolization.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: PAS-stained histologic section of human renal tissue from a patient with atheroembolic renal disease showing cholesterol emboli within fibrotic interstitium with surrounding foreign body giant cells, classic diagnostic manifestations of the disease. B: H&E-stained histologic section of human renal tissue from a patient with atheroembolic renal disease showing cholesterol emboli occluding a renal artery, a classic diagnostic manifestation of the disease, with associated background chronic renal changes noted in the case text.
